title: The Trump-Xi Summit Leaves Taiwan in Limbo
gist: At the September 24 White House summit Xi Jinping pressed Trump to move closer to Beijing's position on Taiwan, and public accounts show no US agreement — consistent with the 'strategic stability' approach US de facto ambassador Raymond Greene outlined in Taipei. The open question is whether Trump can keep dealing with Xi while sustaining deterrence that makes Taiwan harder to conquer.

insights.claim: At the September 24 White House summit Xi Jinping pressed Washington to move closer to Beijing's position on Taiwan, but public accounts show no US agreement to his request.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: No formal US shift on Taiwan — removes an immediate downside catalyst for Taiwan risk assets.

insights.claim: The measure of Trump's cross-Strait policy is now whether he can keep negotiating deals with Xi while making Taiwan harder to conquer; sustained deterrence remains unresolved.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Watch Taiwan arms sales and US Indo-Pacific posture as indicators of whether deterrence is traded for deals.

insights.claim: US de facto ambassador to Taiwan Raymond Greene called for a US-China relationship based on 'strategic stability' and 'fairness and reciprocity' that avoids misunderstandings and miscalculations.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Signals the administration prioritizes managed stability with Beijing over confrontation.
insights.locator: Speaking at the Taipei Security Dialogue

insights.claim: Greene said Washington is reinforcing its presence and partnerships across the Indo-Pacific to maintain a 'favorable regional balance of power'.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Continued US regional force posture supports allied defense spending themes.
insights.locator: Speaking at the Taipei Security Dialogue

insights.claim: Greene praised Taiwan's investments in self-defense and asymmetric capabilities, arguing that to deter conflict Taiwan does not need to show it can win a war outright.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: US encouragement favors Taiwan spending on drones, missiles and other asymmetric systems over big platforms.
insights.quote: to deter a conflict, Taiwan doesn't need to demonstrate that it can win a war outright.
